rv.q: The plot is likely to mystify anyone who’s not an ardent devotee of both Meat Loaf and J M Barrie — a smallish constituency, I’d guess.
Bonkers it may be but, hell, it’s pretty brilliant too.
As an overall experience, however, even for those of us who aren’t devotees, it’s thrilling.
This is Polec’s debut and he is sensational, exuding confidence, making his cartoony character work.
The best musicals have a compelling storyline, thrilling stage pictures and astonishing sounds. This show completely lacks the first, but what swagger and songs it has.
As a spectacle, ‘Bat Out of Hell’ is batshit crazy, often in a good way.
What a bonkers, black-clad, doom-laden night of Wagnerian schlock this is.

That experience — electrifying and giddy and guaranteed to tap into every playgoer’s inner rock god — can be had through Aug. 22 at the capacious Coliseum, where the Jim Steinman musical “Bat Out of Hell” is all but blasting an adoring audience out of their seats.
So, if you love your rock’n’roll, you’ll love this.
It does all equate to a night that will make your jaw drop, your heart soar and have you singing along.
It sounds completely bonkers, and it is completely bonkers.

But if this show marks a massive degradation from those giddy heights of theatrical excellence, I must also openly acknowledge that there is a market for this kind of pop rock spectacle, though it may not be for me.
Sort that out and Bat Out Of Hell gets the five stars it deserves.

A meticulously crafted production, 40 years in the making from writer Jim Steinman, each scene subtly tips its hat to the iconic singer himself – from the wistful waving of a red handkerchief to dramatic unbuttoning of a frilled white shirt – making it one of the most enjoyable and fan-pleasing performances on stage this summer.

cn.t: Critics find this Meat Loaf jukebox musical a gloriously excessive rock spectacle—thrilling fans with its bombastic energy and electrifying performances, though some note the plot is thin and the show borders on ridiculous camp.
